candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XV.6. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness'. Ephrem reads Abraham's faith as the proto-justifying faith — the pattern that Paul will universalise in Rom 4 and Gal 3. Ephrem emphasises that the faith is in a PROMISE (innumerable descendants from a sterile body), not in present visible evidence — establishing faith as TRUST in the divine word against contrary appearance. Tewahedo soteriology preserves the Abrahamic-pattern as the model of saving faith, with Ephrem's emphasis on faith-against-appearance as the monastic-spiritual continuation of this pattern.
